# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## 1. BY PRIMARY MECHANIC

### 1.1 Loop/Path Drawing
*Draw a single continuous loop or path through the grid*

#### 1.1.1 Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** — Loop through black/white circles with turning constraints
- **Slitherlink** — Loop on grid edges with numeric adjacency constraints
- **Mid-loop** — Loop where black circles are midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** — Directional loop with wind constraints

#### 1.1.2 Loop with Regional Constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop through regions; white circles all straight or all turning per region
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop alternates between moon/sun symbols across rooms
- **Suraromu** — Loop passes through numbered gates in order

#### 1.1.3 Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** — Loop plus placed black cells; arrow clues count black cells in a direction

#### 1.1.4 Path Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect island nodes with 1–2 bridges; all connected

---

### 1.2 Cell Shading / Painting
*Determine which cells are black (shaded) and which are white*

#### 1.2.1 Shading with Connectivity Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form one connected wall; white islands match given sizes; no 2×2 black
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers count visible white cells; black cells non-adjacent; whites connected
- **Kurotto** — Circle numbers indicate sum of adjacent black cell groups
- **Heyawake** — Room-based shading; whites can't span 3+ rooms in a line; blacks non-adjacent
- **Nurimisaki** — White "promontory" cells with one white neighbor; no 2×2 of either color
- **Nurimeizu** — Shading creates a maze from S to G with room-level all-or-nothing coloring
- **Norinori** — Exactly two black cells per region, each part of a domino
- **Nuritwin** — Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected

#### 1.2.2 Shading Forming Rectangles
- **Choco Banana** — Black groups must be rectangles/squares; white groups must not be
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles

#### 1.2.3 Shading with Gravity/Physics
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped" they fill the bottom half of the grid

#### 1.2.4 Shading with Deception
- **Usowan** — Numbers count adjacent shaded cells, but one number per room is a liar

#### 1.2.5 Tile-Based Shading
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles (regions) or not; diagonal clue cells give row/column black counts
- **LITS** — Place one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent; all connected

---

### 1.3 Number/Symbol Placement
*Fill cells with numbers or symbols according to constraints*

#### 1.3.1 Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** — Fill 9×9 grid; each row, column, and 3×3 box contains 1–9
- **Hitori** — Black out duplicates so no number repeats in any row/column; whites connected

#### 1.3.2 Region-Based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** — Divide grid into polyomino blocks; each cell shows block size; same-size blocks non-adjacent
- **Ripple Effect** — Rooms get consecutive numbers from 1; same numbers in a line must be spaced apart
- **Makaro** — Rooms filled 1 to N; arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; no same-number adjacency across rooms
- **Nansuke** — Place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-style grid

#### 1.3.3 Directional Symbol Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill cells with — or |; territory clues give majority count; limited consecutive runs
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs; numbered cells count adjacent bulbs; all white cells illuminated; no bulb-to-bulb visibility

---

### 1.4 Grid Division / Partitioning
*Divide the grid into regions or blocks satisfying constraints*

#### 1.4.1 Rectangular Partitioning
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area

#### 1.4.2 Fixed-Size Partitioning
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes; border clue numbers count surrounding block edges

#### 1.4.3 Shape-Constrained Partitioning
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-shapes

#### 1.4.4 Polyomino Partitioning with Chaining
- **Chained Block** — Black cell blocks with size numbers; blocks chain diagonally; unique shapes per chain

---

### 1.5 Object Placement / Movement
*Place or move discrete objects within the grid*

#### 1.5.1 Placement with Line-of-Sight
- **Akari** *(also in 1.3.3)* — Light bulbs illuminate rows/columns
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (1–5 sequences) with visibility/territorial constraints

#### 1.5.2 Movement / Relocation
- **Satogaeri** — Move numbered circles within countries; one circle per country; paths don't cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; sums must match

#### 1.5.3 Progressive Placement
- **Evolomino** — Place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths; each block adds one cell to the previous
- **Pencils** — Mark pencil shapes and draw lines from tips through cells matching pencil numbers

---

## 2. BY CONSTRAINT TYPE

### 2.1 Numeric Clues
| Constraint Style | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Adjacency count** | Akari, Slitherlink, Shakashaka, Usowan, Five Cells |
| **Region sum/count** | Heyawake, Nurikabe, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Norinori, Choco Banana |
| **Visibility/line-of-sight count** | Kurodoko, Yajilin, Akari, Nurimisaki |
| **Block size** | Fillomino, Shikaku, Chained Block, Sashigane, Double Choco |
| **Sequence/order** | Suraromu, Hebi, Ripple Effect, Makaro |
| **Path length** | Satogaeri, Pencils, Yosenabe |
| **Segment midpoint** | Mid-loop |

### 2.2 Connectivity Requirements
| Requirement | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Single connected loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **All white cells connected** | Hitori, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Heyawake, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Nurimeizu |
| **All black/shaded cells connected** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **All islands connected (bridges)** | Hashiwokakero |
| **Paired paths** | Numberlink |

### 2.3 Non-Adjacency / Separation
| Requirement | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Black cells non-adjacent orthogonally** | Hitori, Kurodoko, Yajilin, Heyawake, Usowan |
| **No 2×2 black square** | Nurikabe, LITS, Sto-stone, Nurimisaki |
| **No 2×2 white square** | Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu |
| **Same-size blocks non-adjacent** | Fillomino |
| **Same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent** | LITS |
| **Same-number non-adjacent across rooms** | Makaro |

---

## 3. BY GRID ELEMENT USED

### 3.1 Dots/Vertices
- Slitherlink (lines between dots)

### 3.2 Cell Centers
- Most puzzles (shading, numbers, loops through cells)

### 3.3 Cell Edges/Borders
- Five Cells, Shikaku, Sashigane, Double Choco, Chained Block (partitioning borders)

### 3.4 Circles/Symbols as Clues
- Masyu (black/white circles), Kurotto (numbered circles), Nurimisaki (circles), Satogaeri (movable circles), Yosenabe (movable circles), Hashiwokakero (island circles), Mid-loop (black circles), Dotchi-Loop (black/white circles)

### 3.5 Arrows as Clues
- Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Sashigane, Evolomino, Nagareru

### 3.6 Bold-Lined Rooms/Regions
- Heyawake, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Norinori, Nuritwin, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Double Choco, Nurimeizu, Suraromu, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Satogaeri, LITS, Chained Block

---

## 4. BY OUTPUT TYPE

| What You Produce | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **A closed loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **Open paths** | Numberlink, Pencils |
| **Bridges/edges** | Hashiwokakero |
| **Black/white cell pattern** | Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Heyawake, Norinori, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Choco Banana, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Hitori, LITS, Shakashaka, Akari, Yajilin |
| **Numbers in cells** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Hebi |
| **Symbols in cells** | Juosan (— or \|) |
| **Grid partition** | Shikaku, Five Cells, Sashigane, Double Choco, Chained Block |
| **Object movement arrows** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Polyomino placement** | Evolomino, LITS |

---

## 5. VISUAL SUMMARY TREE

```
Grid-Based Logic Puzzles
├── DRAW (loops, paths, bridges)
│   ├── Closed Loops
│   │   ├── Edge-based: Slitherlink
│   │   └── Cell-based
│   │       ├── Pure: Masyu, Mid-loop
│   │       ├── Regional: Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu
│   │       ├── Directional: Nagareru
│   │       └── Hybrid (loop + shading): Yajilin
│   ├── Open Paths: Numberlink, Pencils
│   └── Bridges: Hashiwokakero
│
├── SHADE (black/white determination)
│   ├── Connectivity-focused: Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Heyawake, Nurimisaki,
│   │                          Nurimeizu, Hitori, Usowan
│   ├── Region-count: Norinori, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Kurotto
│   ├── Shape-constrained: Choco Banana, Shakashaka, LITS, Tilepaint
│   └── Illumination: Akari
│
├── FILL (numbers/symbols in cells)
│   ├── Latin-type: Sudoku, Hitori
│   ├── Block-number: Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro
│   ├── Crossword-number: Nansuke
│   ├── Sequential: Hebi
│   └── Binary symbol: Juosan
│
├── DIVIDE (partition grid into regions)
│   ├── Rectangles: Shikaku
│   ├── Fixed-size: Five Cells
│   ├── L-shapes: Sashigane
│   ├── Matched pairs: Double Choco
│   └── Chained blocks: Chained Block
│
└── MOVE/PLACE (objects in grid)
    ├── Movement: Satogaeri, Yosenabe
    └── Progressive placement: Evolomino
```
